thread.title: Be Fearful Of Netflix When Others Are Greedy - Netflix, Inc. (NASDAQ:NFLX)

author: Dilantha De Silva
title: Be Fearful Of Netflix When Others Are Greedy - Netflix, Inc. (NASDAQ:NFLX)
text:
Overview Netflix ( NFLX ) is a massive success story, and the company has so far led the charge in cut the cord movement. Backed by a stellar subscriber growth rate, both in the U.S. and internationally, Netflix has been able to become a household name across the globe.
(Source – Statista )
The stellar growth in subscribers, eventually resulted in Netflix earning billions of dollars in revenue, and millions in profits, and soon became one of the most followed stocks in the market. Not surprisingly, Netflix stock has surged 465% in the last 05 years.
(Source – Morningstar)
However, industry dynamics are changing, and Netflix will be up against renowned names in the tech and entertainment industry. Considering these new developments and Netflix's financial health, I believe investors need to be fearful of investing in Netflix at the current market price. Netflix is a very attractive company, but the current valuation multiples do not reflect the expected headwinds.
Growth story of Netflix – How Netflix became the media giant it is today The growth story of Netflix starts from the growth in the Over-the-top (OTT) industry, which has been one of the most successful industries in the last decade. Along with technological developments, consumers were demanding more personalized content and the ease of signing up or cancelling subscriptions from their couch, which paved the way for OTT service providers to become mainstream businesses.
OTT video service subscribers worldwide (in millions)
(Source – Statista )
Growth in OTT service subscribers can be attributed to below factors.
OTT services are cheaper than traditional cable-TV packages. OTT subscription services do not generally have a contract period, and consumers can enjoy multiple subscriptions at the same time and cancel any one of those subscriptions at their discretion, without incurring any penalties. OTT subscription services offer the much needed touch of personalization to consumers which was lacking. Rapid development in information technology, and the increased number of people with access to internet on a global basis. From being a DVD mailing service, Netflix has grown into the most admired streaming service provider in the world.
From being a streaming company with a focus on licensing top quality content from existing big names in the industry, Netflix has developed into one of the most sought after content creation companies in the world. Netflix has already released hundreds of original TV shows and movies which were monumental in the success story of the company. Original content has been the huge driving force behind the massive growth of subscribers.
On the other hand, Netflix provided the much-needed convenience to consumers. Netflix has clearly capitalized on their first-mover advantage and has expanded in to hundreds of countries across the globe , which has positioned the company as a tough-to-beat player in the streaming industry.
More recently, Netflix has focused on creating content using local languages, which is expected to mark another important chapter in Netflix’s growth story.
All in all, Netflix looks a wonderful company, but the real question is whether this wonderful company is trading at an attractive level of valuation.
Future outlook of Netflix – increasing challenges Netflix definitely has the potential to grow in the coming years, and the industry is also poised for growth. However, in my opinion, it would be irrational to assume that future growth will be as spectacular as the past growth based on a few reasons. In addition, financial performance and health of the company should also be closely evaluated to determine strengths and weaknesses of Netflix.
Analysis of Growth opportunities outside the U.S.
Netflix benefited immensely from the eruption of popularity in OTT services in the last 6 years, but such growth might cease to exist in the future. This is not to claim that there won’t be growth opportunities in the future, but the company might fail to grow at the same pace it did in the past. As per latest available data, 59% of adults in the U.S. have already subscribed to Netflix, which leaves little room for Netflix to grow in the U.S., which currently accounts for around 60% of company revenues.
Revenue growth in the U.S. is expected to decelerate
(Source – Forbes )
One argument for the continued growth of Netflix is the opportunities available outside the U.S., which has been highlighted and talked about in the recent past. Therefore, one needs to consider whether these growth opportunities can be materialized.
Success of Netflix outside the U.S. will depend not only on the company’s ability to establish a name in Asian markets, but also on the development of technology. The company is already looking at India as a massive growth opportunity, but, in my opinion, it would be extremely difficult for Netflix to replicate what they did in the U.S. in India.
Internet speeds in Asian countries are considerably lower than in the U.S. and developed countries, which forms the first barrier for Netflix. Even though infrastructure related to the communications sector has advanced steadfastly over the last couple of decades, Asian and Latin American countries are well behind the developed world.
(Source – Atlas and Boots )
Active internet users in Asian countries have increased steadily, but, even then, less than 50% of total population in the region has access to internet. On the other hand, many Asian countries have Fair User Policies (FUP) that limits the number of GBs a user can utilize without taking a hit on the internet speed.
Below chart exhibits how internet penetration improved in Asia over the last decade but continued to remain below the world average.
(Source - Statista )
Moving on from relatively low internet speeds and penetration rates, the next big obstacle for Netflix is pirated movies and TV shows. In my view, pirated content poses a major threat for the success of Netflix in Asian and Latin American countries as there are massive loop-holes in legislative activities against pirated content in these countries.
(Source – Tech in Asia )
As expected, close to two thirds of the population in the developed world have never used pirated video content, whereas more than two thirds of the population in the developing world are watching pirated content. These industry characteristics are mostly left out of the analysis when evaluating the growth prospects of Netflix outside the U.S., which is a costly mistake in my opinion.
As mentioned earlier, India remains one of the most important target markets, not only for Netflix, but also for other OTT video streaming services. However, there are unique characteristics in the Indian market, and international players, including Netflix, are struggling against local competitors.
(Source – Statista )
Even though Netflix has been able to successfully gain viewership in India, I believe the company will have to spend billions of dollars more on creating local content to make a meaningful impact in this market. This is where things might start going south for Netflix as return on these investments will be far lower than what the company experienced in the U.S. In addition, increased competition from both local and international players in India might result in Netflix paying a significant premium to acquire content from local content providers.
The Latin American market is another focus area for Netflix and the OTT video streaming industry is expected to blossom in this market. While Netflix was enjoying a virtual monopoly in the OTT space since 2011 in Latin America, local pay-TV providers have now realized the threat posed by Netflix and have been quick to respond to this threat by introducing their own OTT video streaming platforms. Most of these services are value additions to existing pay-TV subscribers. In line with this, competition in the industry is expected to significantly increase in Latin America as well and inherent issues such as low internet penetration and slow internet speeds will continue to pose challenges to Netflix.
On the other hand, China is one of the major potential markets for any content streaming company, but regulations in China do not allow Netflix or any other international player to establish a presence in China. Deep-pocketed local players will continue to dominate the OTT video streaming industry in China, which can be seen from the most recent data available.
(Source – eMarketer )
Overall, there is certainly room for Netflix to grow outside the U.S., and the company management should be given credit for identifying these opportunities and pursuing such growth aggressively. However, there are inherent risks in spending billions of dollars to expand outside the U.S., leading to the conclusion that growth outside the U.S. will not be as smooth as it was in the U.S.
Increasing competition
As the first-mover to the industry, Netflix was able to enjoy a dominant position in the OTT video streaming market in the U.S. for so long, and the company has successfully leveraged such benefits in outside markets as well. So far, Amazon Prime (NASDAQ: AMZN ) and Hulu have been the major rivals of Netflix, but these companies have not been able to pose a meaningful threat to Netflix.
(Source – CNBC )
Moving on, competition for Netflix will not stem from niche players in the industry but from other tech giants who have access to significant levels of capital and user data. Netflix’s soaring success can be attributable to a few factors, but access to data and user behavior remains one of the main driving forces behind the success of Netflix. This would be put to test in the near future when companies that store massive amounts of user data such as Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), and Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) enter the industry.
Netflix, so far, has operated more like a monopoly, and its huge library of content has been a massive differentiator between its peers. However, moving forward, I believe the industry will become much more competitive, and there will be a group of players who will provide considerably advanced streaming solutions to consumers than what Netflix’s current peers provide.
In 2019 and beyond, renowned names in the tech and entertainment industry are set to unveil OTT platforms, which, in my opinion, remains the single biggest threat to Netflix’s competitive advantage.
Key competitors to look out for in 2019 and beyond
Company
Future prospects
Facebook
Facebook Watch is in its infant stage but has already gained traction. The massive active monthly user base of around 2 billion will surely help Facebook build on the viewer base. Facebook has already purchased rights to broadcast few major sports leagues and is expected to expand its horizons by acquiring more broadcasting rights for sports events. The massive, multi-billion dollar cash balance, is one of its many advantages, which would naturally be useful in acquiring or creating original content.
Apple
Apple is already spending billions of dollars on purchasing and creating content, and the release of a streaming platform appears to be closer than ever. With billions of devices sold worldwide and a second to none brand value, coupled with billions of dollars in cash, Apple is poised to make a major break-through in the streaming industry. The readily available user-base to market its platform provides Apple with an edge to gain traction in the streaming industry at a faster clip than most of its potential rivals.
Amazon
Amazon Prime Video is the closest competitor of Netflix at the moment and is closely tied to the Amazon Prime membership, which will drive the popularity of the streaming platform in the future. Amazon Prime Video has already established a user base in India which would be a major catalyst in competing with its rival, Netflix. Though Amazon could not be of a meaningful challenge to Netflix in the U.S., the situation will surely be different outside the U.S. As Netflix’s future growth story lies outside the U.S., Amazon is poised to become a major threat as the company will most likely price their offering at a very attractive rate than Netflix, backed by its billion dollar business and its intention to market Prime Video as a complementary service to Amazon Prime members.
Disney
Disney (NYSE: DIS ) is all set to launch Disney+ in the latter half of this year which will house original content from Disney, Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars. Disney has already made their intentions clear on creating original content surrounding their iconic characters, which will pose a major threat to existing industry players. In addition, Disney might cease selling their movies to Netflix, which would certainly become an obstacle for Netflix to remain the industry leader.
YouTube
YouTube TV is still in the very early stages, but the subscriber base has been growing throughout 2018. Even though YouTube is making losses in this front, it is currently working on bringing in more TV channels to its platform. In addition, YouTube TV will certainly focus on creating original content , and it has the luxury of pushing the service in front of billions of users and possibly adapt an advertisement based model which will help gain traction in a competitive market.
Cable-TV providers
Cable-TV providers have been hit hard by the rise of Netflix and the OTT video streaming industry. Most cable-TV providers are now focusing on negating the threat posed by Netflix by introducing their very own OTT video streaming platforms. While these efforts have not been able to present a major threat to Netflix so far, I believe this will change in the future as these companies understand the industry dynamics on a more broad level. Their existing user base will help a smooth transition from a cable only model to a blended model with an OTT video streaming platform, which would be a catalyst for growth in the future.
(Source - Author prepared based on data from company filings and conference call transcripts)
Netflix’s subscriber-based business model has gained massive popularity in the Americas and Europe, but the company might want to re-consider deploying such a model in Asian countries as consumers in this region are much more cautious in discretionary spending and are very sensitive to price hikes. Facebook Watch has adopted an advertisement based model, which can be expected to yield better results in gaining viewership outside the U.S. Even though Apple has not come up with a model, they might choose to go for an advertisement based model as well, knowing that non-U.S. markets are becoming increasingly important to the success of a content streaming service. These developments will threaten the success of Netflix in Asia and other developing regions, which should be incorporated in assigning a growth rate for the company.
On the other hand, the threat posed by Facebook, Apple and YouTube in the Asia-Pacific region cannot be compared with data from Americas.
For an example, video streaming accounts for 56% of all traffic on the internet, and who controls this space varies from region to region.
(Source – Sandvine )
While the Americas is dominated by Subscription Video on Demand (SVOD) services, the Asia-Pacific region is populated by social media and advertisement based platforms. While SVOD is still in its early stage in this region, it would be irrational to predict that SVOD will gain market share at the same pace it did in the Americas.
Billions of dollars spent on content
For the fiscal year 2018, the company has so far spent more than $9 billion on content, which is expected to reach $13 billion for the full year. Netflix has three core reasons to increase its spending on original content.
Original content has fueled Netflix’s growth story so far and is expected to remain a key factor in attracting a loyal customer base. Entertainment giants, including Disney, are focusing on introducing their very own OTT video streaming platforms, and Netflix needs to be ready for this by maintaining a healthy pipeline of original content. Growth outside the U.S. can only be achieved if Netflix continues to create original content in local languages. On the other hand, consumers’ expectations on Netflix are seemingly high. Users expect Netflix to come up with top-notch original content on a regular basis, which is the exact same reason why millions of users tend to continue their subscription with Netflix.
However, there would be certain implications in spending billions of dollars on content to keep a competitive advantage in the future. Along with massive spending on content, Netflix was able to build on its subscriber base at a rapid pace. However, billions of dollars spent in creating original content in other languages to attract users from around the world will not yield Netflix as much as it did when they ramped up spending on creating original content with the target of acquiring subscribers in the U.S. While this poses a threat to Netflix’s continued profitability, investors should not forget that the company will most probably be competing with deep-pocketed rivals for market share.

All of Netflix’s future rivals are looking financially healthier than Netflix, which brings the sustainability of Netflix’s business model into question. However, admittedly, Netflix still has to continue with this model despite looming risks.
Next, we should compare Netflix’s ability to generate free cash flow with its potential rivals' ability to generate free cash flow.
(Source - Author prepared with Morningstar data)
Clearly, all the other companies are far superior in generating free cash flow in comparison with Netflix. One argument against this thesis is that Netflix can easily turn its free cash flow from negative to positive by cutting down its aggressive spending on original content. However, if this happens, competitors will be all over Netflix, and the company will start losing its loyal customer base. This is the next big dilemma the company has to face in the future, and there is an increased risk of Netflix spending more than it could afford for content, which would be helpful in securing short-term profits, but not long-term sustainability.
Absence of switching costs
The presence of switching costs is a value driver for a company, especially in a macro-economic environment in which competition is heating up. Users would evaluate upcoming services on a cost to value basis, if switching costs exist. However, in the absence of switching costs, users would be more inclined to switch to other service providers to test their services.
From what we can see from the latest developments, Netflix’s biggest competitors will most likely adopt an advertisement based business model, which provides all the more reason for existing Netflix subscribers to try these services. This does not immediately pose a threat to Netflix as users can of course keep their Netflix subscriptions alive, but in the long-run, this trend will drag customers away from Netflix to its rivals on the assumption that these rivals will come up with appealing original content.
Conclusion – lack of identifiable catalysts for 2019 Netflix is certainly a success story and the company has grown from renting DVDs to become the leading player in the billion dollar streaming industry. Aggressive growth strategies implemented by the company management were instrumental in Netflix’s success and the industry-wide growth played its part.
The future outlook for the industry looks promising as more and more people shift toward OTT video streaming instead of cable-TV subscriptions. Under the prevailing macro-economic conditions, one would naturally expect the industry leader to experience a massive surge in profitability and revenue, but increased competition stemming from large-scale tech and entertainment players is expected to have a negative effect on the profitability of Netflix.
Growth prospects do not look bleak for the company, but it would be optimistic to expect the company to grow at the same level it did in the last decade as the company focuses on markets outside the U.S.
During the latter part of 2019, many of Netflix’s rivals are expected to roll out video streaming platforms which would surely spark concerns about the company’s future profitability. Notably, these companies look healthier than Netflix from the perspective of financial health as well.
Netflix for sure is a very attractive company, operating under favorable macro-economic conditions, but 2019 might turn out to be a tough year for Netflix as there are no identifiable catalysts to support the growth story. Rather, all available data points to a deterioration of company fundamentals in the latter half of this year. Therefore, even though I believe Netflix is an attractive company, I do not believe the price is right to make an investment.
